extracted.intended_audience: NIH applicants, peer reviewers, and NIH staff involved in Research Project Grant (RPG) review and submission
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policy describing NIH's simplified peer review framework for most Research Project Grant (RPG) applications, explaining what reviewers should focus on and how applicant-facing processes are affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key question — Should the proposed research project be conducted?
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the proposed research project be conducted?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The simplified framework explicitly directs peer reviewers to focus on answering this high-level question as part of assessing the scientific and technical merit of proposed research projects. This is intended to help identify the strongest, highest-impact research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key question — Can the proposed research project be conducted?
rubrics_metrics.description: Can the proposed research project be conducted?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers are expected to focus on the feasibility of conducting the proposed work when assessing scientific and technical merit. This complements the 'should' question to judge both potential impact and practicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of Investigator and Environment (refocused)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigating the effect of reputational bias by refocusing the evaluation of investigator/environment to within the context of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the simplified framework, assessments of the investigator(s) and institutional environment are to be contextualized specifically with respect to the proposed research project rather than relying on broader reputation. This is intended to reduce reputational bias in review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift policy compliance activities to NIH staff (reduce reviewer burden)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reducing reviewer burden by shifting policy compliance activities to NIH staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy compliance checks that previously may have fallen to reviewers will be handled by NIH staff, allowing reviewers to concentrate on the scientific and technical merits (the 'should' and 'can' questions). This is a procedural change affecting reviewer responsibilities rather than application content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on identification of strongest, highest-impact research
rubrics_metrics.description: The simplified peer review framework aims to better facilitate the mission of scientific peer review — identification of the strongest, highest-impact research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and NIH staff should prioritize selection of projects with the greatest potential impact. The framework is designed to refocus review activities to support this mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability / Implementation timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with January 25, 2025 due dates, NIH implemented a simplified framework for the peer review of the majority of competing research project grant (RPG) applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes the effective date and scope of the policy: most competing RPG activity codes are subject to the simplified framework starting with the specified due dates. Applicants and reviewers should use guidance and resources tied to this implementation timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on application content vs. funding opportunity selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the simplified review framework has little impact on what is included in an application, it does have significant impact on the funding opportunities used to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are informed that application forms/content largely remain unchanged, but they must pay attention to which funding opportunity announcements and activity codes are using the simplified framework. Applicant Guidance pages provide practical navigation assistance.
